item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Hypnotic

lookback_source.quote: N0415D1. Hypnotic: Check if a hypnotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period ending on the ARD, or since admission/entry or reentry if the stay is less than 7 days. The manual uses the terms "7-day look-back period" (N0415D1) and "observation period" (N0415D2) interchangeably for this item; the column header on the item table states "during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days." No other time window is stated for this item.

coding_levels.label: Hypnotic — Is taking
coding_levels.definition: Check if a hypnotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415D1. Hypnotic: Check if a hypnotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Hypnotic — Indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all hypnotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415D2. Hypnotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all hypnotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Is taking / Indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Column 1: check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification, not how it is used, during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days. Column 2: if Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification, not how it is used, during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415D1 if a hypnotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415D1. Hypnotic: Check if a hypnotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415D2 only if there is an indication noted for ALL hypnotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415D2. Hypnotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all hypnotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (indication noted) is coded only if Column 1 is checked.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in N0415 by therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not by use; e.g., oxazepam prescribed as a hypnotic is coded as antianxiety, not as a hypnotic.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used. For example, although oxazepam may be prescribed for use as a hypnotic, it is categorized as an antianxiety medication.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Over-the-counter sleeping medications are not coded as hypnotics because they are not categorized as hypnotic medications.

source.quote: Over-the-counter sleeping medications are not coded as hypnotics, as they are not categorized as hypnotic medications.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root) are not counted as medications for this item.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification must be coded in all assigned categories/classifications, regardless of how the medication is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly are counted only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication for N0415 only if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A hypnotic taken PRN during the look-back period is checked in N0415D1; N0415D2 is left unchecked when the indication for its use was not noted (example: temazepam given PRN with no indication documented).

source.quote: N0415D1. Hypnotic = checked; temazepam is a hypnotic medication. N0415D2. Hypnotic = not checked; indication for use of temazepam was not noted.

federal.criterion: Medical record documentation that the medication was received by the resident and documentation of the indication for its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Steps for Assessment step 1 for N0415.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Steps for Assessment step 2 for N0415.

federal.criterion: The indication must be an identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: DEFINITIONS box: INDICATION. Supports coding of Column 2 (N0415D2).

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0 pharmacological classification (facilities may identify a consistent classification resource; the package insert or the resident's pharmacist may be consulted).

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish to") with an expectation that assessors can identify the source used.

federal.criterion: When a resident receives antipsychotic, antianxiety and hypnotic medications simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication for their use; adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use.

source.quote: Please note: if a resident is receiving medications in all three of these high-risk drug classes simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication for the use of these medications.

federal.notes: Same page adds: "Adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use."

federal.criterion: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed reference resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415D (Hypnotic) to any payment or case-mix classification.
